Context: pages 62-64 obtain identities by comparing coefficients in an earlier partial-fraction identity (21) for the case αβ=π². A sister identity (22) handles αβ=π²/4. Eq. (24) on p.62 is the coefficient of 1/x, (25)-(26) the coefficients of 1/x^r, and (28) the coefficient of x^r. This page finishes (28), gives the x^0 case (29), and begins the sech family (30).

(28), concluded. Assume αβ=π² and r≥2 is an integer.
- First rewrite (mine, certain): Σ_{k≥1} k^{1-2r}/(e^{2kα}-1) = Σ_{n≥1} σ_{1-2r}(n) e^{-2nα}.
- So (4α)^{1-r}{½ζ(2r-1)+Σ_n σ_{1-2r}(n)e^{-2nα}} − (−4β)^{1-r}{½ζ(2r-1)+Σ_n σ_{1-2r}(n)e^{-2nβ}} equals a Bernoulli polynomial in α and β.
- That polynomial is:
  |B_{2r}|/(2r)!·{(−α)^r+β^r}
  + π²|B_2||B_{2r-2}|/(2!(2r-2)!)·{(−α)^{r-2}+β^{r-2}}
  − π⁴|B_4||B_{2r-4}|/(4!(2r-4)!)·{(−α)^{r-4}+β^{r-4}} + …
- Signs alternate as (−1)^{j+1} for the j-th pair, j≥1.
- Ramanujan uses B_2=1/6, B_4=1/30, … (absolute values).
- The last term is −π^r (B_r/r!)²(−1)^{r/2} if r is even. If r is odd it is π^{r-1}·B_{r-1}/(r-1)!·B_{r+1}/(r+1)!·(−1)^{(r+1)/2}(β−α).

My reduction to the modern form. Put n=r−1 and modern signed B_k. The page is then exactly 4^{-n} times Ramanujan's formula:
 α^{-n}(½ζ(2n+1)+Σ k^{-2n-1}/(e^{2αk}-1)) − (−β)^{-n}(…β…) = −2^{2n} Σ_{j=0}^{n+1} (−1)^j B_{2j}B_{2n+2−2j}/((2j)!(2n+2−2j)!) α^{n+1−j}β^j.
The steps are:
- Use αβ=π² to write α^{r−j}β^j = π^{2j}α^{r−2j}.
- Pair term j with term r−j to get the brackets {(−α)^{r−2j}+β^{r−2j}}.
- The unpaired middle term (r even) or the last pair (r odd) gives the stated 'last term'.
Example, r=2, α=β=π: Lerch's ζ(3)=7π³/180 − 2Σ 1/(k³(e^{2πk}−1)).

(29). Equate terms independent of x in (21); this is the excluded r=1 case. Using Σ 1/(k(e^{2kα}−1)) = Σ σ_{−1}(n)e^{−2nα}, with αβ=π²:
 F(α) − F(β) = ¼ log(α/β) − (α−β)/12.
My derivation:
- F(α) = −α/12 − log η(iα/π).
- Use η(−1/τ) = √(−iτ) η(τ) with τ=iα/π, so that −1/τ = iβ/π.
- This gives F(α)−F(β) = ½ log(α/π) − (α−β)/12.
- Since α/π = √(α/β), this equals ¼ log(α/β) − (α−β)/12.
So (29) is the Dedekind eta transformation.

(30). This comes from (22). With αβ=π²/4 and r≥1:
 α^r Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^k (2k+1)^{2r−1}/cosh((2k+1)α) + (−β)^r Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^k (2k+1)^{2r−1}/cosh((2k+1)β) = 0.
My reformulation:
- Expand sech x = 2Σ_m (−1)^m e^{−(2m+1)x}.
- The sum becomes 2Σ_{n odd} χ_{−4}(n)σ_{2r−1}(n)e^{−nα}; this is (31) on the next page.
- This is a weight-2r Eisenstein series for Γ0(16) with character pair (χ_{−4},χ_{−4}).
- The map α↦π²/(4α) is the Fricke involution τ↦−1/(16τ), with q=e^{2πiτ}=e^{−α}.
- So (30) states the Fricke eigenvalue is −1, and there is no constant-term correction.
Special case α=β=π/2, r even: Σ (−1)^k (2k+1)^{2r−1} sech((2k+1)π/2) = 0. For odd r the case α=β=π/2 is trivial.
The page ends 'In other words', leading to the σ-form (31) on p.64.
errors: No mathematical errors found: (28)'s right side matches Ramanujan's ζ(2n+1) formula term by term, including signs and both 'last term' cases. (29) matches the eta transformation. (30) is consistent with the modular structure.
Notational points only. B_k denotes the unsigned Bernoulli numbers |B_k|. In the odd-r last term, B_{r−1} and B_{r+1} have even indices (Ramanujan's indexing), which is consistent.
'r is any positive integer excluding 0' is redundant wording. The derivation from (21)/(22) by 'equating coefficients' presupposes an expansion that is not shown on this page.

results.what: Transformation formula for ζ(2r−1) plus Lambert-type series under αβ=π², written in σ_{1−2r} form with explicit Bernoulli last terms (eq. 28)
results.modern_name: Ramanujan's formula for ζ(2n+1) (Lerch's ζ(3) formula as a special case)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (second notebook Ch.14 Entry 21(i); lost notebook); ζ(3) case Lerch 1901; proofs by Grosswald, Berndt

results.modern_name: Dedekind eta function transformation η(−1/τ)=√(−iτ)η(τ), logarithmic form
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1877 (also Schlömilch); appears in Ramanujan's notebooks

results.modern_name: Transformation of the weight-2r Eisenstein series Σ χ_{−4}(n)σ_{2r−1}(n)q^n (Fricke involution on Γ0(16)); sech-sum analogues of Ramanujan's formula
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan's notebooks (Ch.14 analogues); classical special cases (vanishing at α=π/2) known to Cauchy/Glaisher-era authors

deep.surprise_reason: All results are the well-known Ramanujan transformation formulas (ζ(2n+1) formula, eta transformation, sech-series analogues) recorded in his notebooks and studied extensively by Berndt et al. The page is a manuscript version with a careful pairing of Bernoulli terms, which is of moderate archival interest only.

transcription_corrections: 'equating the terms independent of r' should read 'independent of x': the comparison is of powers of x in (21), and the handwritten letter is the same x/n-like glyph used for x elsewhere.
Ramanujan's ζ is written as a looped 'ʃ'-like symbol; it is correctly rendered as ζ(2r−1).
In (29) the denominators are written '1(e^{2α}−1)', '2(e^{4α}−1)', i.e. k(e^{2kα}−1); the transcription is correct.
